components.gap: Durrett's Theorem 4.6.2 (printed p. 245) assumes only phi >= 0 with phi(x)/x -> infinity and E phi(|X_i|) <= C for every i; it assumes no integrability, and its conclusion (uniform integrability in his sense, p. 244, which yields sup E|X_i| <= M + 1) includes integrability. The handbook defines uniform integrability only for families of real integrable random variables (body lines 17-18), and thm:p15-ui-moment-criteria (body lines 48-51) neither says that no integrability is assumed nor derives it: the annex proof (lines 36-46) bounds only the tails E(|X_i|; |X_i| > M_eps) <= eps C and never shows E|X_i| < infinity (for example E|X_i| <= M_eps + eps C). As written, the entry either presupposes integrability, narrowing the source hypothesis, or concludes it without a written step. Supply the unrestricted variant: state that the moment bound alone suffices and add the integrability step to the annex proof.
